guarantees.claim: ready_o, ctr_we_o, alert_o are forced to 0 as initial defaults; aes_ctr_ns, ctr_slice_idx_d, ctr_carry_d are initialized to their current registered values before case overrides.
In state CTR_IDLE, ready_o is asserted and alert_counter_d is cleared to 0.
In CTR_IDLE, if incr_i == 1, then ctr_slice_idx_d is set to 0, ctr_carry_d to 1, and next state becomes CTR_INCR.
In CTR_INCR, ctr_slice_idx_d is incremented by 1, ctr_carry_d is assigned from ctr_value[SliceSizeCtr], and ctr_we_o is asserted.
In CTR_INCR, when ctr_slice_idx_q equals all-ones (max slice index), the next state is set to CTR_IDLE.
In CTR_ERROR, if alert_counter_q < 100, alert_counter_d is incremented and alert_o remains 0; otherwise alert_counter_d is unchanged and alert_o is set to 1 (delayed alert after 100 cycles).
For any state other than CTR_IDLE, CTR_INCR, or CTR_ERROR, the FSM forces next state to CTR_ERROR and immediately asserts alert_o.
Regardless of current state, if incr_err_i or mr_err_i is high, aes_ctr_ns is forced to CTR_ERROR, overriding any other transition.

assumptions.claim: incr_err_i and mr_err_i must be glitch-free and stable; a glitch will cause a false entry to CTR_ERROR, eventually asserting alert_o permanently after 100 cycles.
assumptions.risk: Spurious alert assertion, potential denial-of-service and masking of real errors.

assumptions.claim: When ctr_we_o is asserted (in CTR_INCR), the external logic providing ctr_value[SliceSizeCtr] must supply a valid carry-out bit for the current slice.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect carry bit leads to wrong counter value, breaking the counter integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: A transient assertion of incr_err_i or mr_err_i (even a single-cycle pulse) latches the FSM into CTR_ERROR with no exit path. After 100 cycles, alert_o goes high and stays high, causing an irreversible alert from a transient event.
uncertain_points.risk: Permanent system fault response from a hardware glitch, threatening availability.

uncertain_points.claim: If the state machine enters an invalid state (e.g., via malicious glitch or SEU), the default branch immediately asserts alert_o (bypassing the 100-cycle counter) and transitions to CTR_ERROR. The comment indicates this is intentional for security, but a non-malicious transient fault could trigger an unwarranted immediate alert.
uncertain_points.risk: Immediate alert from a non-malicious bit-flip may cause a false system-wide reaction; design intent needs clarification.

uncertain_points.claim: In CTR_IDLE, alert_counter_d is reset to 0. Because there is no transition from CTR_ERROR back to CTR_IDLE, this reset is unreachable after the FSM has ever entered CTR_ERROR. The purpose of resetting the counter in IDLE is unclear.
uncertain_points.risk: No functional impact, but may indicate a missing error recovery path or leftover code.
